summary.text: 上 is an indicative graph: a small mark above a reference line indicates the upper side. Early forms are described with either a curved or horizontal line. Shang-period inscriptional uses are reported, including 上帝 and 上甲.

formation.text: The mark’s position above a reference line indicates the upper side. The received Shuowen text also classifies 上 as indicative; this records a Han-era analysis, not independent confirmation of the graph’s earlier history.

history.text: Early forms are described as a short mark above a longer reference line, though accounts differ on whether the line was curved or horizontal. Later forms altered the upper mark, often making it vertical to distinguish 上 from 二; the modern standard form has a dot. These are graphic changes, not evidence of a change in meaning.

The received Shuowen text treats 丄 as an ancient form meaning “high” and 上 as its seal-script form. Received editions differ over whether the head form is 丄 or 二; this is a difference in the transmitted lexicographic tradition, not confirmation of Shang graphic history.

uncertainties.text: The earliest graph form discussed is oracle-bone 上, but no earlier dated occurrence is established. Paleographic accounts report inscriptional examples; a photograph of an artifact transcribed with 上甲 does not isolate that character.
Accounts agree on a mark above a reference line but differ on whether the early line was curved or horizontal; no primary inscription image resolves this variation.

Reported uses include spatial “above/upper side” and “at/on the side of,” authority-related meanings, and verbs glossed “ascend” and “send up.” The evidence does not establish a dated sequence or semantic connections among these uses. The reported 以上 meaning “more than” is a compound use, not evidence for a single-character sense.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone and Zhou bronze inscription contexts reported
senses.text: Reported Shang-period examples include 上帝, 上甲, and contrasts with 下; Zhou bronze examples include spatial “above.” These support early spatial uses but do not establish priority among every lexical use.
Bronze-inscription accounts report this spatial use. Its relationship to “above” is not established.
Current dictionary definitions include spatial and rank-related meanings; their historical sequence is not established.

limitations.text: Early spatial uses are supported, and several other uses are reported, but dated semantic transitions among them are not established. 上帝 and 上甲 are compound examples, not automatically independent senses of 上.

The reported 以上 example means “more than” in a compound and does not establish a single-character sense. Supplied reconstructed phonological rows separately gloss 上 as “ascend,” “put up,” and “top, above”; these rows do not establish attested usage, semantic chronology, or graphic origin.

overview.text: A small mark above a reference line indicates the upper side. 上 is used for “above,” “upper,” and “superior.”

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern vector rendering, not a dated artifact
items.caption: This Shuowen seal-script-style rendering has an upper stroke that bends right and descends into a central upright, above a long horizontal baseline. It illustrates a received seal-style form without establishing a dated transition from an earlier graph.
items.alt: A black glyph with a long horizontal baseline, a central upright, and an upper stroke that curves right and down into the upright.
items.selection_reason: The rendering provides a useful example of 上 in Shuowen seal-script style. Its visible form is distinct from the simple upper mark and reference line described for early forms, but it does not establish a historical sequence between them.
